title: TerraUY Evidence Grounding Benchmark (TEGB): Trustworthy Reasoning over Earth Observation Evidence
description:
TerraUY Evidence Grounding Benchmark (TEGB) — Trustworthy Reasoning over Earth Observation Evidence. v0.1 — Research Preview. An open research benchmark with reproducible results; not peer-reviewed.

TEGB evaluates whether AI agents respect what Earth Observation evidence supports — and what it does not establish. v0.1 contains 82 tasks (74 in 10 failure families plus 8 affirmative controls), three evidence conditions (RAW, TEXT, STRUCTURED), and an initial baseline of four models: 2,952 responses scored by two blind LLM judges (5,904 verdicts) and a deterministic detector, with preregistration, evaluation harness, reproduction scripts and a technical report.

Pooled unsupported conclusion rate: RAW 50.8%, TEXT 17.4%, STRUCTURED 20.9%. Explicit evidence semantics reduced unsupported conclusions by 33.4 percentage points (95% CI [−38.5, −28.3], paired p < 0.001); structured JSON did not improve grounding over equivalent natural-language constraints (+3.6 pp, 95% CI [0.1, 6.9], p = 0.007).

Validation status. TEGB v0.1 has not yet undergone independent expert human review. The primary results are based on two blind model judges, deterministic checks, paired statistical analysis and multiple sensitivity analyses. A blind robustness review was also performed using ChatGPT-generated assessments adopted by the project owner; this is not treated as independent human validation.
